zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Rūm
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الم﴾ ﴿غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ﴾ [al-Rūm: 2] — we have already explained what has come concerning ”الـم“. It has been read ”غُلِبَتْ“, with ḍamma on the ghayn, and Abū ʿAmr read ”غَلَبَتْ“, with fatḥa on the ghayn. [Translator's note: the attribution of the active reading «غَلَبَتْ» to Abū ʿAmr is as in the source; this reading is usually reported as non-canonical and from others.] The meaning is according to ”غُلِبَتْ“ (were defeated), and it is the consensus of the readers; that is because Persia had defeated the Byzantines at that time, and the Byzantines were defeated, so the reading is ”غُلِبَتْ“.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ كانَ عاقِبَةَ الَّذِينَ أساءُوا السُّوأى أنْ كَذَّبُوا﴾ — the reading is with ”عاقِبَةَ“ in the accusative and in the nominative. Whoever reads the accusative makes ”اَلسُّوءى“ the noun (ism) of ”كانَ“, and whoever reads ”عاقِبَةُ“ in the nominative makes ”اَلسُّوءى“ the khabar (predicate) of ”كانَ“. The interpretation of His saying ”أساؤُوا“ here is that they associated partners [with Allah], and ”اَلسُّوءى“ is the Fire. ”أساؤُوا“ here indicates shirk only because of His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النّاسِ بِلِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكافِرُونَ﴾ [al-Rūm: 8]; so their evil-doing here is their unbelief, and the recompense of unbelief is the Fire. What also indicates that ”أساؤُوا“ here is unbelief is: ﴿أنْ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ وكانُوا بِها يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾. So the meaning is: "Then the end of the unbelievers was the Fire, because of their denial of Allah's signs and their mockery."

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُبْلِسُ المُجْرِمُونَ﴾ — Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that on the Day of Resurrection they will be cut short in argument, with the cutting short of those who despair of Allah's mercy. ”اَلْمُبْلِسُ“ is the one who falls silent, cut short in his argument, despairing of finding his way to it. You say ”ناظَرْتُ فُلانًا فَأبْلَسَ“ (I debated so-and-so and he was struck dumb), i.e. he was cut short, held back, and despaired of arguing.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السّاعَةُ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَفَرَّقُونَ﴾ — it has come in the tafsīr that it is a separation after which there is no gathering. And in what follows it there is an indication that the separation is between the Muslims and the unbelievers; so He said: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يَتَفَرَّقُونَ﴾.

zajjaj:15-15.t: Then He made clear in what state they will be separated, and said: ﴿فَأمّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ فَهم في رَوْضَةٍ يُحْبَرُونَ﴾. It has come in the tafsīr that ”يُحْبَرُونَ“ is listening to singing in Paradise. ”اَلْحَبْرَةُ“ in the language is every fine blessing; it is a ”حَبْرَةٌ“. ”اَلتَّحْبِيرُ“ is making beautiful. ”اَلْحَبْرُ“, the learned man, is also from this; the meaning is that he is adorned with the finest character of the believers. And ”اَلْحِبْرُ“ is ink; it was so named only because things are made beautiful with it.

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿وَأمّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا ولِقاءِ الآخِرَةِ فَأُولَئِكَ في العَذابِ مُحْضَرُونَ﴾ — i.e. "The state of the believers is listening [to song] in Paradise and being occupied with the utmost blessing, and the state of the unbelievers is the painful punishment, which they attend forever, without it being lightened for them."

zajjaj:17-17.t: Then, after this, He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that by which Paradise is attained and by which one is kept far from the Fire, with His saying: ﴿فَسُبْحانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ﴾ ﴿وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ وعَشِيًّا وحِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ﴾ [al-Rūm: 18]. It has come in the tafsīr from Ibn ʿAbbās that the proof that the prayers are five is this verse: ”فَسُبْحانَ اللَّهِ حِينَ تُمْسُونَ وحِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ“. So ”حِينَ تُمْسُونَ“ is the sunset prayer and the late-evening prayer (ʿishāʾ al-ākhira); ”حِينَ تُصْبِحُونَ“ is the morning prayer; ”عَشِيًّا“ is the afternoon (ʿaṣr) prayer; and ”حِينَ تُظْهِرُونَ“ is the noon (ẓuhr) prayer. It has also been said that His saying ﴿وَمِن بَعْدِ صَلاةِ العِشاءِ ثَلاثُ عَوْراتٍ لَكُمْ﴾ [al-Nūr: 58] — that it is the fifth prayer; so according to this interpretation His saying ”حِينَ تُمْسُونَ“ would be for a single prayer. The meaning of ”سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ“ is declaring Allah free of every evil; there is no disagreement about this.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُخْرِجُ الحَيَّ مِنَ المَيِّتِ ويُخْرِجُ المَيِّتَ مِنَ الحَيِّ﴾ — it has come in the tafsīr that He brings forth the sperm-drop — which is the dead — from the living, from the human being; and ”وَيُخْرِجُ الحَيَّ مِنَ المَيِّتِ“: He brings forth the human being from the sperm-drop. ﴿وَيُحْيِي الأرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها﴾ — i.e. He makes it put forth vegetation; and the reviving of the earth is bringing forth plants from it.
His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ﴾ — i.e. and likewise you will be brought out of your graves, resurrected. The position of the kāf is accusative by ”تُخْرَجُونَ“, and the meaning is that your resurrection, for Him, is like your creation, i.e. the two are equal in His power.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن آياتِهِ أنْ خَلَقَكم مِن تُرابٍ﴾ — i.e. among the signs that indicate that Allah is One, without any like, is the manifestation of the power which created beings are incapable of. The meaning of ”خَلَقَكم مِن تُرابٍ“ is "He created Adam from dust"; ﴿ثُمَّ إذا أنْتُمْ بَشَرٌ تَنْتَشِرُونَ﴾ — i.e. Adam and his offspring.

zajjaj:21-21.t: ﴿وَمِن آياتِهِ أنْ خَلَقَ لَكم مِن أنْفُسِكم أزْواجًا لِتَسْكُنُوا إلَيْها﴾ — He created Ḥawwāʾ from one of the ribs of Adam. Affection and mercy between wife and husband are placed from Allah, and al-fark — which is hatred — is from Satan. One says ”فَرِكَتِ المَرْأةُ زَوْجَها، تَفْرِكُهُ، فِرْكًا“ when she hates him.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿فِي أدْنى الأرْضِ﴾ — it has been said: in the outlying parts of Syria; and its interpretation is: "the nearest land to the land of the Arabs."
His saying: ﴿وَهم مِن بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ﴾ ﴿فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ﴾ [al-Rūm: 4] — this is among the verses that indicate that the Qur'an is from Allah, because it foretold what was going to happen, and this is known only to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. The idolaters had been delighted that Persia had defeated the Byzantines; that was because they said: "You, O Muslims, claim that you will be given victory because you are people of a Book. Persia has defeated the Byzantines, and Persia are not people of a Book while the Byzantines are people of a Book; so likewise we shall defeat you." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the Byzantines would be victorious within a few (biḍʿ) years and that the Muslims would rejoice at that. So the Muslims made a wager with the idolaters and contracted with them over the truth of this report. ”اَلْبِضْعُ“ is what lies between three and nine. When part of the biḍʿ had passed, the idolaters demanded [payment] from the Muslims and said: "We have beaten you, because a few years have passed and the Byzantines have not defeated Persia." The Muslims argued against them that the biḍʿ had not been completed; they raised [the stake] for them and deferred them until the completion of the biḍʿ. Then the Byzantines defeated Persia and the Muslims won the wager — that was before gambling was forbidden — and the Muslims rejoiced and the unbelievers were disgraced.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِلَّهِ الأمْرُ مِن قَبْلُ ومِن بَعْدُ﴾ [al-Rūm: 4] — the reading is with ḍamma; the people of Arabic hold to it, and the readers are all agreed upon it. As for the grammarians, they permit ”مِن قَبْلٍ ومِن بَعْدٍ“ with tanwīn, and some of them permit ”مِن قَبْلِ ومِن بَعْدِ“ without tanwīn, and this is an error. For ”قَبْلُ“ and ”بَعْدُ“ here are originally in the genitive, but they were made indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma because they are two ghāyas ("terminals"). The meaning of "ghāya" is that the word has had its genitive complement (iḍāfa) deleted, and what remains after the deletion is made the end (ghāya) of the word. They were made indeclinable on ḍamma only because their inflection in construct is the accusative and the genitive: you say ”رَأيْتُهُ قَبْلَكَ، ومِن قَبْلِكَ“ (I saw him before you, and from before you), and they are not put in the nominative, because nothing is predicated of them, since they are used as two adverbs (ẓarf). So when they were turned away from their proper category, they were vowelled with a vowel other than the two vowels that used to enter them by right of inflection. As for the necessity of their losing their inflection and being made indeclinable, it is because they became definite by a route other than [the usual means of] definiteness, since what they were annexed to was deleted from them. The meaning is: "To Allah belongs the command before the Byzantines were defeated and after they were defeated." As for the genitive with tanwīn, it is according to one who makes them both indefinite; the meaning is: "To Allah belongs the command from precedence and from succession (min taqaddumin wa-taʾakhkhur)." And the ḍamma is better. As for the kasra without tanwīn, al-Farrāʾ mentioned that it is left as it would be in construct, without tanwīn, and he cited as evidence the words of the ancient poet:
بَيْنَ ذِراعَيْ وجَبْهَةِ الأسَدِ
(between the two forearms and the forehead of the Lion [constellation])
and his saying:
إلّا غُلالَةَ أوْ بَداهَةَ قارِحٍ نَهْدٍ الجُرارَةْ
(except the second run or the first burst of a full-grown, sturdy horse of great stride)
But this is not like that, because the meaning of ”بَيْنَ ذِراعَيْ وجَبْهَةِ الأسَدِ“ is "between its two forearms and its forehead," so one of the two terms to which they are annexed has been mentioned. Thus, if it were ”لِلَّهِ الأمْرُ مِن قَبْلِ ومِن بَعْدِ كَذا“, it would be permissible and the meaning would be "before such-and-such and after such-and-such." This view is not one to be given any consideration, and none of the early grammarians held it.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِن بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ﴾ — ”اَلْغَلَبُ“ and ”اَلطَّلَبُ“ are two maṣdars (verbal nouns): you say ”غَلَبْتُ غَلَبًا“ (I overcame, an overcoming) and ”طَلَبْتُ طَلَبًا“ (I sought, a seeking). One of the grammarians claimed that it was originally ”مِن بَعْدِ غَلَبَتِهِمْ“, and mentioned that when the iḍāfa occurred the hāʾ of ”غَلَبَة“ was dropped. This is an error: ”اَلْغَلَبَةُ“ and ”اَلْغَلَبُ“ are [both] maṣdars of ”غَلَبْتُ“, like ”اَلْجَلَبُ“ and ”اَلْجَلَبَةُ“.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿وَعْدَ اللَّهِ لا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ وعْدَهُ﴾ — the reading is the accusative in ”وَعْدَ“; the nominative is permissible, and the accusative is permissible, but I do not know of anyone who read it in the nominative. The accusative is on the basis that it is an emphasising maṣdar (verbal noun), because His saying ﴿وَهم مِن بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ﴾ [al-Rūm: 3] is a promise from Allah to the believers, and His saying ”وَعْدَ اللَّهِ“ is equivalent to "Allah promised a promise." Whoever says ”وَعْدُ اللَّهِ“, it is in the sense of "That is the promise of Allah," just as He said: ﴿كَأنَّهم يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَ ما يُوعَدُونَ لَمْ يَلْبَثُوا إلا ساعَةً مِن نَهارٍ بَلاغٌ﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 35].

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ ظاهِرًا مِنَ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾ — this concerns the idolaters of the people of Mecca. The meaning is: "They know of the livelihoods of the life of this world," because they were engaged in trade. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, when He negated [their knowledge], made known that they do not know what it is they are ignorant of, and the extent of what they know, and He said: ﴿يَعْلَمُونَ ظاهِرًا مِنَ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا وهم عَنِ الآخِرَةِ هم غافِلُونَ﴾. The first ”هم“ is nominative by being the mubtadaʾ (subject); the second ”هم“ is a second mubtadaʾ, and ”غافِلُونَ“ is the khabar (predicate) of the second ”هم“; and the second clause is the khabar of the first ”هم“. The benefit in the speech, or in mentioning ”هم“ a second time — even though it is a mubtadaʾ — is that it is treated like tawkīd (emphasis), just as you say ”زَيْدٌ هو عالِمٌ“ (Zayd, he is learned), which is more emphatic than your saying ”زَيْدٌ عالِمٌ“ (Zayd is learned). It is also valid for ”هم“ to be a badal (substitute) of the first ”هم“, likewise emphasising, as you say ”رَأيْتُهُ إيّاهُ“ (I saw him, him).

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا في أنْفُسِهِمْ ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ وما بَيْنَهُما إلا بِالحَقِّ﴾ — its meaning is: "Have they not reflected, and so come to know?!", because there is an indication of it in the speech. The meaning of ”بِالحَقِّ“ here is "only for the truth," i.e. for establishing the truth; ﴿وَأجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾, i.e. "for establishing the truth and for a named term," which is the time in which every soul will be paid in full what it earned.
His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ النّاسِ بِلِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكافِرُونَ﴾ — i.e. "are surely disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord." The bāʾ was placed first because it is connected to ”كافِرُونَ“, and what is connected to the khabar (predicate) of ”إنَّ“ may be placed before the lām; but the lām may not enter after the khabar has passed: you may not say ”إنَّ زَيْدًا كافِرٌ لَبِاللَّهِ“, because the lām's proper place is to enter upon the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar, or between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar, since it emphasises the clause; so it does not come as an emphasis once the clause has passed. There is no disagreement among the grammarians that the lām does not enter upon anything other than the khabar.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأثارُوا الأرْضَ وعَمَرُوها أكْثَرَ مِمّا عَمَرُوها﴾ — He means that those of the bygone nations who were destroyed had more tillage and cultivation than the people of Mecca, because the people of Mecca were not people of tillage.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن آياتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ البَرْقَ خَوْفًا وطَمَعًا﴾ — ”خَوْفًا وطَمَعًا“ are both accusative as mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); the meaning is: "He shows you the lightning for fear and hope" — it is fear for the traveller and hope for the one at home. The meaning is: "And among His signs is a sign by which He shows you the lightning, in fear and hope." This is better as regards the conjunction, because He said: ﴿وَمِن آياتِهِ خَلْقُ﴾ [al-Rūm: 22], so He conjoined a noun to a noun. Similar to it in poetry is:
وَما الدَّهْرُ إلّا تارَتانِ فَمِنهُما ∗∗∗ أمُوتُ وأُخْرى أبْتَغِي العَيْشَ أكْدَحُ
(Time is nothing but two spells: in one of them I die, and in the other I seek a living, toiling.)
The meaning is: "of the two there is a spell in which I die (أُمُوتُها)", i.e. "I die in it." And it is possible that the meaning is: "And He shows you the lightning, in fear and hope, [as one] of His signs," so it would be the conjoining of a clause to a clause.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِن آياتِهِ أنْ تَقُومَ السَّماءُ والأرْضُ بِأمْرِهِ﴾ — i.e. the sky stands without pillars, and likewise the earth stands by His command, and the sky encompasses it.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ إذا دَعاكم دَعْوَةً مِنَ الأرْضِ﴾ — i.e. for the resurrection after death.

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَهُ مَن في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ كُلٌّ لَهُ قانِتُونَ﴾ — its meaning is: obedient. The meaning is: "And this is among His signs"; He did not mention "وَمِن آياتِهِ" because it had already been mentioned several times. The meaning of ”قانِتُونَ“ is: obedient with an obedience alongside which no disobedience can occur, because ”اَلْقُنُوتُ“ is standing in obedience. The meaning of obedience here is that in the creation of those who are in the heavens and the earth there is proof that they are created by the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; no one is able to change the creation, not even an angel brought near is able to do so. So the traces of the making and the creation indicate obedience. He does not mean the obedience of the servants [in worship]; it is only the obedience of [submission to His] will and wish.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ الخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وهو أهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ﴾ — there is more than one view about it. Among them: that the hāʾ refers back to the creation, so the meaning is: "the restoration and resurrection are easier for the human being than his original production," because in coming into being he endures what he does not endure in the restoration and resurrection. Abū ʿUbayda and many of the people of the language said that its meaning is: "and it is easy (hayyin) for Him," and that ”أهْوَنُ“ here does not mean that the restoration is easier for Him than the beginning, because the restoration and the beginning are each easy for Him. Of this kind in poetry is:
لَعَمْرُكَ ما أدْرِي وإنِّي لِأوْجَلُ ∗∗∗ عَلى أيِّنا تَغْدُو المَنِيَّةُ أوَّلُ
(By your life, I do not know — and I am truly afraid — which of us death will come upon first.)
So the meaning of ”لَأوْجَلُ“ is ”لَوَجِلٌ“ (truly afraid). And they said ”اَللَّهُ أكْبَرُ“, i.e. "Allah is great (kabīr)," and that is not disapproved. Better than these two aspects is that He addressed the servants with what they understand: He made known to them that by their own reckoning the resurrection must be simpler and easier than the beginning and the original production, and He made it a likeness (mathal) for them; so He said: ﴿وَلَهُ المَثَلُ الأعْلى في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ — i.e. His saying ﴿وَهُوَ أهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ﴾ He has struck for you as a likeness concerning what is difficult and what is easy.

zajjaj:28-28.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿ضَرَبَ لَكم مَثَلا مِن أنْفُسِكم هَلْ لَكم مِن ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُكم مِن شُرَكاءَ في ما رَزَقْناكُمْ﴾ — this is a likeness which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, struck for whoever assigns Him a partner from among His creation. So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that a man's slave is not his partner in his wealth and his wife, and that he does not fear that his slave will inherit from him. So He said: "He has struck for you a likeness from yourselves, in that you made what is Allah's property among His creation like Allah, while you are all human beings, and your slaves are not on a par with you in your wealth; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is more worthy that His creation should not be made equal to Him." ﴿كَذَلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ الآياتِ﴾ — the position of the kāf is accusative.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأقِمْ وجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا﴾ — ”اَلْحَنِيفُ“ is the one who inclines towards something and does not turn back from it, like ḥanaf in the foot, which is its inclining outward by natural constitution; the one with ḥanaf cannot correct his ḥanaf.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النّاسَ عَلَيْها﴾ — ”فِطْرَةَ اللَّهِ“ is accusative in the sense of "follow the fiṭra of Allah," because the meaning of ”فَأقِمْ وجْهَكَ“ is "follow the upright religion, follow the fiṭra of Allah." The meaning of ”فِطْرَةَ اللَّهِ“ is "the natural make-up given by Allah, upon which He created humankind." As for the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «كُلُّ مَوْلُودٍ يُولَدُ عَلى الفِطْرَةِ حَتّى يَكُونَ أبَواهُ يُهَوِّدانِهِ ويُنَصِّرانِهِ ويُمَجِّسانِهِ» ("Every child is born upon the fiṭra until his parents make him a Jew, a Christian or a Magian"), its meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, created creation upon faith, according to what has come in the ḥadīth: that Allah, exalted be His praise, brought forth from the loins of Adam his offspring like tiny particles and made them bear witness over themselves that He is their Creator. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَإذْ أخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَنِي آدَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهم وأشْهَدَهم عَلى أنْفُسِهِمْ ألَسْتُ بِرَبِّكم قالُوا بَلى﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 172]. So every child born is from that offspring which bore witness that Allah is its Creator. So the meaning of ”فِطْرَةَ اللَّهِ“ is "the religion of Allah upon which He created people."
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ﴾ — most of what has come in the tafsīr is that its meaning is "there is no altering the religion of Allah," and what follows it indicates this, namely His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ الدِّينُ القَيِّمُ ولَكِنَّ أكْثَرَ النّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾, i.e. they do not know the reality of that.

zajjaj:31-31.t: His saying: ﴿مُنِيبِينَ إلَيْهِ﴾ — ”مُنِيبِينَ“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), by His saying ﴿فَأقِمْ وجْهَكَ﴾ [al-Rūm: 30]. All the grammarians held that the meaning of this is "So set your faces, turning to Him in repentance," because the community is included with the Prophet ﷺ in an address to him; the proof of that is His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 1]. His saying ”مُنِيبِينَ“ means: returning to Him, to everything He commanded, not departing from anything of His command. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known to them that the straight way in the religion of Islam is following the fiṭra, and piety together with Islam, and the performance of the obligations, and that this does not benefit except with sincerity in tawḥīd; so He said: ﴿وَلا تَكُونُوا مِنَ المُشْرِكِينَ﴾ ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ﴾ [al-Rūm: 32] — and it has been read ”فارَقُوا دِينَهم“ (who parted from their religion) — ﴿وَكانُوا شِيَعًا﴾ [al-Rūm: 32], i.e. sects. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded them to unite, to be in harmony, and to hold to the community (jamāʿa); and the Sunna lies in guidance, and misguidance is division.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾ — i.e. every faction of this group, those who parted from their religion, is rejoicing, thinking that it is the rightly guided one.

zajjaj:33-33.t: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that when harm touches them they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance, i.e. in their hardships they do not take refuge with those whom they worshipped alongside Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; they return in their supplication to Him alone. ﴿ثُمَّ إذا أذاقَهم مِنهُ رَحْمَةً إذا فَرِيقٌ مِنهم بِرَبِّهِمْ يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ — i.e. when He lets them taste mercy by delivering them from that hardship in which they called upon Allah alone, after that they carry on in their shirk.

zajjaj:34-34.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَكْفُرُوا بِما آتَيْناهم فَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — the sense of ”فَتَمَتَّعُوا“ is an address after a report, because when He said ”لِيَكْفُرُوا“ it was a report about absent persons; so the meaning is: "So enjoy yourselves, you who do this, for you will come to know." This is not a binding command which Allah gave them; it is a command by way of threat and menace. That is used in people's speech: you say, "If you let me hear something hateful, I will do and deal with you," and then you say, "Do such-and-such to me, for you will see what befalls you." If he does not let you hear [it], he is not thereby disobeying you; this is proof that it is not a binding command. Likewise ﴿فَمَن شاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن ومَن شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾ [al-Kahf: 29], and likewise ﴿اعْمَلُوا ما شِئْتُمْ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 40]: they were not given a free choice between faith and unbelief; rather it follows the manner of addressing the servants, and the discourse of the Arabs which they use to intensify a threat. Do you not see that after ﴿فَمَن شاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن ومَن شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾ [al-Kahf: 29] He says ﴿إنّا أعْتَدْنا لِلظّالِمِينَ نارًا أحاطَ بِهِمْ سُرادِقُها﴾ [al-Kahf: 29]? This is among what confirms that it is a threat.

zajjaj:38-38.t: His saying: ﴿فَآتِ ذا القُرْبى حَقَّهُ والمِسْكِينَ وابْنَ السَّبِيلِ﴾ — Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, assigned a right to the near relative, and likewise to the poor; and ”اِبْنُ السَّبِيلِ“ (the wayfarer) is the guest, so He made hospitality obligatory. As for relatives, the laws of inheritance have made clear what is due to each category of them, and it is as though the shares of inheritance have abrogated this — I mean the matter of the right of kinship. And it is possible that kinship has a binding right in [matters of] kindness.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿وَما آتَيْتُمْ مِن رِبًا لِيَرْبُوَ في أمْوالِ النّاسِ فَلا يَرْبُو عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ — He means by it a person's giving something in order to be compensated with what is more than it. According to most of the tafsīr that is not forbidden, but there is no reward for one who gets back more than he gave [Translator's note: so in the source, «لِمَن زادَ عَلى ما أخَذَ», literally "for one who added to what he took"]. Ribā is of two kinds. The forbidden is every loan through which more than it is taken, or which draws a benefit; this is forbidden. That which is not forbidden is what a person gives as a gift, seeking thereby what is more than it, or the present he gives, seeking thereby what is more than it.
His saying: ﴿وَما آتَيْتُمْ مِن زَكاةٍ تُرِيدُونَ وجْهَ اللَّهِ﴾ — i.e. whatever charity you give not seeking repayment by it, but they only intend by it what is with Allah; ”فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ المُضْعَفُونَ“, i.e. its people are the ones multiplied, i.e. they are the ones for whom the reward is multiplied: they are given ten times the like for a good deed, and Allah multiplies for whom He wills. It has also been said ﴿المُضْعِفُونَ﴾, as one says ”رَجُلٌ مَقْوٍ“, i.e. possessed of strength, and ”مُوسِرٌ“, i.e. possessed of wealth; likewise ”مُضْعِفٌ“, i.e. possessed of multiples of good deeds.

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ”ظَهَرَ الفَسادُ في البَرِّ والبَحْرِ بِما كَسَبَتْ أيْدِي النّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهم بَعْضَ الَّذِي عَمِلُوا“ — and it is also read with yāʾ: ﴿لِيُذِيقَهُمْ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; both forms quoted are with yāʾ — the first quotation was presumably meant as «لِنُذِيقَهم», with nūn]. I.e. that He may make them taste the recompense of some of their deeds. Its meaning: drought appeared on land, and dearth at sea, i.e. in the cities of the sea, i.e. in the cities that are on rivers; and everything that has water is a "sea" (baḥr).

zajjaj:43-43.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأقِمْ وجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ القَيِّمِ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا مَرَدَّ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ﴾ — the meaning of ”فَأقِمْ وجْهَكَ“ is: set your aim straight, and make your direction the following of the upright religion, before the Hour comes and the Resurrection takes place, when no soul's faith will benefit it if it had not believed before or earned some good through its faith. The meaning of ”يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ“ is: they will separate, becoming a party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلأنْفُسِهِمْ يَمْهَدُونَ﴾ — i.e. they are preparing [a resting place] for themselves.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أرْسَلْنا رِيحًا فَرَأوْهُ مُصْفَرًّا﴾ [al-Rūm: 51] — i.e. they saw the vegetation had turned yellow and dried up; ﴿لَظَلُّوا مِن بَعْدِهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ [al-Rūm: 51] — and its meaning is ”لِيَظَلُّنَّ“ (they would surely remain) [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the intended form is presumably «لَيَظَلُّنَّ»], because the sense of the speech is condition and recompense. So they rejoice at the rain, and disbelieve when the rain is cut off from them and the vegetation dries up.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُهُ كِسَفًا﴾ — i.e. pieces of cloud.
His saying: ﴿فَتَرى الوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِن خِلالِهِ﴾ — i.e. you see the rain coming out from the gaps of the cloud. So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He produces the clouds, revives the earth and sends the winds, and all that is proof of the power which created beings are incapable of, and that He is able to give life to the dead.

zajjaj:49-49.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَإنْ كانُوا مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يُنَـزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن قَبْلِهِ لَمُبْلِسِينَ﴾ — the meaning is "before the rain is sent down upon them"; and it is read ”أنْ يَنْزِلَ“ (before it comes down). The meaning of ”مُبْلِسِينَ“ is: cut short with the cutting short of those who despair. As for the repetition of His saying ”مِن قَبْلِ“, there are two aspects in it. Quṭrub said: the first ”قَبْلِ“ is for the sending down, and the second ”قَبْلِ“ is for the rain. Al-Akhfash and others of the Basrans said: the repetition of ”قَبْلِ“ is by way of tawkīd (emphasis), and the meaning is: "and indeed, before the sending down of the rain, they were in despair." The view is as they said, because the sending down of the rain is in the sense of the rain, since rain only comes about through being sent down, just as winds are only known through their passing. The poet said:
مَشَيْنَ كَما اهْتَزَّتْ رِماحٌ تَسَفَّهَتْ ∗∗∗ أعالِيَها مَرُّ الرِّياحِ النَّواسِمِ
(They walked [swaying] as spears quiver whose tops the passing of the gentle breezes has set swaying.)
So the meaning of ”مَرُّ الرِّياحِ“ is like your saying ”تَسَفَّهَتْ أعالِيَها مَرُّ الرِّياحِ النَّواسِمِ“. [Translator's note: the explanation repeats the verse's own wording; the point intended is that "the passing of the winds" stands for "the winds".]

zajjaj:50-50.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فانْظُرْ إلى آثارِ رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ﴾ — and it is read ”أثَرِ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ“ (the trace of Allah's mercy). He means the traces of the rain, which is a mercy from Allah — how He revives the earth after its death, and its revival is His making it put forth vegetation; and likewise is the revival of the dead. So He said: ﴿إنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمُحْيِي المَوْتى﴾ — ”ذَلِكَ“ is a reference to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿فَإنَّكَ لا تُسْمِعُ المَوْتى ولا تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ الدُّعاءَ إذا ولَّوْا مُدْبِرِينَ﴾ — this is a likeness which Allah struck for the unbelievers, as He said: ﴿صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 18]. So He made them, in their failing to act upon what they hear and to heed what they see, as the dead; because what He has made clear of His power and His making, the like of which created beings are not able to do, is proof of His Oneness.

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿إنْ تُسْمِعُ إلا مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِآياتِنا﴾ — i.e. none hears except one who believes in Our signs. He made "causing to hear" here count as causing to hear when it is accepted and what is heard is acted upon; and when it is not accepted it is as what has not been heard and not been seen.
His saying: ﴿وَما أنْتَ بِهادِ العُمْيِ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ﴾ — the reading is with the genitive in ”اَلْعُمْيِ“, and the accusative is permissible: ”بِهادٍ العُمْيَ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ“. The reading is with the genitive. As for the accusative, if there is a transmission for it [then so be it]; otherwise reading with it is not permissible, because anything that is recited without there being a prior transmission for it from the early readers of the cities — reciting with it is an innovation, even if it is permissible in Arabic. The practice in all recitation is following the Sunna.

zajjaj:54-54.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكم مِن ضَعْفٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةً ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ ضَعْفًا وشَيْبَةً يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ﴾ — its interpretation is that He created you from sperm-drops in a state of weakness, then strengthened you in the state of youth, then after youth made weakness and grey hair. It is related in the ḥadīth «that Ibn ʿUmar said: I recited to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكم مِن ضَعْفٍ﴾, and he had me recite ”مِن ضُعْفٍ“. And ʿAṭiyya recited to Ibn ʿUmar ”مِن ضَعْفٍ“, and he had him recite ”مِن ضُعْفٍ“ and said to him: "I recited it to the Prophet ﷺ as ”مِن ضَعْفٍ“,» and he had me recite ”مِن ضُعْفٍ“." So what ʿAṭiyya related from Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet ﷺ is ”مِن ضُعْفٍ“, with ḍamma. It has also been read with fatḥa on the ḍād, and the preferred choice is the ḍamma, because of the transmission.

zajjaj:55-55.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السّاعَةُ يُقْسِمُ المُجْرِمُونَ﴾ — He means the Day of Resurrection. ”اَلسّاعَةُ“ in the Qur'an has the meaning of the hour in which the Resurrection takes place; for that reason He left out any mention identifying which hour it is. ﴿يُقْسِمُ المُجْرِمُونَ﴾ — the criminals swear; ﴿ما لَبِثُوا غَيْرَ ساعَةٍ﴾ — i.e. they did not remain in their graves except a single hour; ﴿كَذَلِكَ كانُوا يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ — i.e. like this lie was their lying [in the world], because they swore without verification.

zajjaj:56-56.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا العِلْمَ والإيمانَ لَقَدْ لَبِثْتُمْ في كِتابِ اللَّهِ إلى يَوْمِ البَعْثِ﴾ — i.e. in the knowledge of Allah, recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿فاصْبِرْ إنَّ وعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ﴾ — i.e. what Allah has promised you of victory over your enemy is true, and the manifestation of the religion of Islam is true. ﴿وَلا يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ الَّذِينَ لا يُوقِنُونَ﴾ — i.e. "Let not those who have no certainty unsettle you from your religion," i.e. they are astray and in doubt.
